vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes are opened at once, whatever the schedule, and still wait for every check.

fedora-stable.description: Fedora releases that Bodhi marks current (stable): never a branched, beta or Rawhide release.

customManagers.description: The Fedora release the image and the providers are built on, in the Containerfiles and in the workflow that records the base digests.
ulogd, built from netfilter.org's tarball in the image: Fedora doesn't package it.
libnetfilter_log, built from netfilter.org's tarball in the image: Fedora's is too old for ulogd.
The Renovate release CI checks this file with.

packageRules.description: Non-major updates merge themselves once every check, the VM suites included, has passed.
Major updates open a pull request each, for review; never merged automatically.
Group non-major Rust crate updates, as Dependabot's rust group did.
Group non-major updates to the web UI's npm packages.
Group GitHub Actions updates; they stay pinned to commit SHAs.
The config validator CI runs goes with the other CI tools.
Angular names the TypeScript releases it supports: a new TypeScript major waits on the dashboard until Angular takes it.

A new ulogd or libnetfilter_log changes the tarball's checksum too, which Renovate can't compute: the build fails at sha256sum until the matching _SHA256 ARG is updated by hand, from the release's signed tarball on netfilter.org.
prBodyNotes: **By hand:** update the matching `_SHA256` ARG in `image/Containerfile` from the release's tarball on netfilter.org (check its signature); until then the image build fails at `sha256sum -c`, by design.

packageRules.description: The UI is built in the image with Fedora's Node.js, and CI uses the same major; it moves with Fedora, not on its own.

Fedora base images: the regex manager above moves them to a new stable release, all in one pull request. The Dockerfile manager would offer any tag on quay.io, branched and Rawhide included. Within a release the tags float on purpose, and the monthly rebuild tracks them.
A new Fedora release is a major OS upgrade: one pull request for every place that names it, through every VM suite, merged by hand.
The Quadlet units name images by placeholders that the build fills in (Image=@KEA_IMAGE@); there is nothing to update.
Commit as build(deps): for every update. Last, so it overrides the fix/chore split that config:recommended applies by dependency type.
